event_text: Maldives to Have Multiparty Democracy. After decades of authoritarian rule, the Maldives will have a multiparty system beginning Sunday. Until now, political parties were banned in the Maldives, a Muslim nation made up of more than 1,100 coral islands off southern India. Thursday, lawmakers voted unanimously for a multiparty system that will allow opposition parties to function for the first time in this Indian Ocean archipelago. Soon after the vote, the government released four opposition politicians who were detained earlier in the day on allegations of plotting to disrupt the parliamentary debate. President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom has ruled the Maldives with an iron fist since 1978. Last year, he promised political reforms following international pressure spurred by allegations of torture of politicians who were jailed after a series of anti-government riots in 2003.

## Event Type: ## Event: **RETREAT**: RETREAT covers any events—not just military “retreat” from territory—which involve concessions and have immediate (not simply promised) material consequences. Promises of future actions do not fall under this category, only actions that have immediate consequences. This category differs from CONCEDE in that concessions are verbal concessions, while RETREAT relates to material concessions.

In general, the entity "retreating" or making material concessions is the ACTOR, while the beneficiary or target of the retreat is the RECIPIENT.

Includes:
- retreat from territory as well as withdrawing forces from an area.
- Release captives
- Return property
- Disarm militarily or give up weapons
- Implement ceasefire (note: this does not include a promise of future ceasefire, just the actual implementation of a ceasefire)
- Allow somone to access territory
- Allow election observers into the country
- Allow peacekeepers into the country
- Allow humanitarian workers to have access"
- A resignation by a government official
## Sub-Events: RETREAT events can include withdraw, release, return, disarm, ceasefire, access, resign
## Potential Ambiguities: - Announcements of future retreats should be coded as CONCEDE. E.g., “announced...would withdraw troops” is RETREAT + FUTURE and should be coded as CONCEDE.
- Debt forgiveness and loan cancellations, e.g. “The Paris Club has agreed to forgive $200 of Nigeria’s $350 million in loan obligations, . . . ” should be coded as AID.
- Hostage rescues, e.g. “Pakistan’s military rescued 10 hostages from the border region with Afghanistan yesterday” or “Police in Barcelona freed 10 human trafficking victims during an
operation yesterday” should be coded as AID.
- Refugees or similar actors that are characterized fleeing a country or subnational location should be coded SANCTION ‘expel’ with the causative agent as the actor rather than SANCTION ‘withdraw’ or RETREAT ‘withdraw’
## Attribute Guidance: ACTOR is the party carrying out the retreat, release, or withdrawal. These are reported in the passive far more often than other types: search the whole document for an explicitly linked mention of the agent before leaving ACTOR empty.

## Event Type: ## Event: **ASSAULT**: ASSAULT events are deliberate actions which can potentially result in substantial physical harm, including violence, battles, or assaults.

Can include:
- Abduct or kidnap people
- hijack planes, buses, or other vehicles
- take prisoners of war during combat
- beating; physically assault by striking individuals or groups with one-off or repeated blows, typically administered manually or by blunt instrument
torture
- Judicially-sanctioned execution
- sexual violence
- Targeted assassinations (both successful and attempted) with any weapon
- Destroy property, demolish as part of a conflict
- Attack someone with primitive weapons: fire, edged weapons, rocks, farm implements
- Use firearms, including rifles, pistols, light machine guns to attack someone.
- Use mines, IEDS, car bombs 
- Use suicide attacks, both individual attacks and suicide car bombings
- Use any manned aerial vehicles, e.g. aircraft, helicopters to carry out an attack. 
- Use unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), drones to carry out an attack
- Attack someone using heavy weapons, including artillery, rocket launchers, armored vehicles, tanks, and similar weapons
- Use "crowd control" weapons, including tear gas, water cannons, firing weapons in the air, lathi charges, etc.
- Engage in mass expulsions or deportations
- Engage in ethnic cleansing
- Instances of mass killing or massacres
- Use of chemical, biological, radiation, and nuclear weapons
- Kill people
- Injure people
## Sub-Events: ASSAULT events can include abduct, beat, torture, execute, sexual, assassinate, destroy, primitive, firearms, explosives, suicide-attack, aerial, drone, heavy-weapons, crowd-control, cleansing, massacre, unconventional
## Potential Ambiguities: In general, PLOVER is not intended to code day-to-day crimes and is meant to focus on "political" violence, although that distinction is difficult to draw in practice. Thus, ordinary murders or street crime would generally not fall under ASSAULT, while violence in the context of conflict between armed groups, terrorism, or political violence would be included.

Lawful arrests are NOT included—covered by COERCE

RECIPIENT is what the text states the attack was directed at: the targets, and only the targets. Keep counts in the span ('26 Iraqi soldiers'). People harmed are never RECIPIENTs when a target is stated, and they do not get a record of their own; when the text states no target and gives only the people harmed, they are the RECIPIENT. When the text states several targets for one attack, each is a separate RECIPIENT list item. Separate attacks in one article are separate records with distinct anchor quotes.

## Event Type: ## Event: **THREATEN**: All threats, coercive or forceful warnings with serious potential repercussions. Threats are generally verbal acts except for purely symbolic material actions such as having an unarmed group place a flag on some territory.

Threaten to ban political activities of particular parties or individuals

Threaten to suspend relations or talks
Threaten to restrict civil rights such as speech, expression, and assembly
Threaten to expel diplomats, peacekeepers, NGOs, etc
Threaten to occupy, seize control of the whole or part of a territory
Threaten violence

event_text: South Africa Probes Police Killing of 34 Miners. A South African judicial commission has launched an investigation into the police killing of 34 striking mineworkers. The three-member panel was due to visit the Lonmin platinum mine in Marikana township, where the deadly shooting took place August 16. The commission, headed by retired Judge Ian Farlam, began its work with a public hearing in Rustenburg on Monday. The investigation is expected to last about four months. The commission will look into the role of different parties in the violence, including police, the striking mineworkers, mineworkers' unions and Lonmin platinum. A total of 45 people were killed during a violent five-week strike at the mine over a pay dispute. The workers eventually won a 22 percent pay increase -- a development that triggered new strikes last week, as other mineworkers demanded wage hikes. President Jacob Zuma appointed the inquiry panel in August. Human Rights Watch urged the government to conduct a broader, independent inquiry to ensure the panel's findings are unbiased.

## Event Type: ## Event: **ACCUSE**: ACCUSE covers a wide range of events, including any kind of accusation, disapproval or criticism, investigation, or legal accusation

Includes

- Express disapprovals, objections, and complaints
- condemn, decry a policy or an action
- criticize, defame, denigrate responsible parties

- Any investigation, including commissions, grand juries, judicial or political. This also includes:
- Investigation of corruption
- Investigation of war crimes or human rights abuses
- Investigations into whether a ceasefire was violated

Making allegations, including
- Formally or informally accuse
- sue in court
- criminally indict
- charge with a crime
- bring to trial (note: this does not include convictions)
## Sub-Events: ACCUSE events can include disapprove, investigate, allege
## Special Instructions: When a person speaks on behalf of an organization the organization is the ACTOR A titled officeholder speaking in their own name is the ACTOR. The RECIPIENT must be a concrete entity. If the only reported target of criticism is a policy, issue, etc, then leave RECIPIENT blank.
## Potential Ambiguities: ACCUSE ‘disapprove’ is used for diplomatic protests, as well as delegations presenting a disagreement to an organization or authority, or protests carried out in social media. As noted under CONSULT, summoning an in-country ambassador to present such grievances is just coded ACCUSE, not CONSULT.

Protests (including protests expressing disapproval) are coded under a separate PROTEST category. Protests DO NOT fall under this category.

Convictions are coded under a separate SANCTION category.

ACCUSE events are distinct from involve warnings, forecasts, or threats.

When an accusation or allegation is also reported alongside a formal conviction, ACCUSE ‘allege’ should not be coded as these are cases where the allegation was proven to be true.
## Attribute Guidance: ACTOR is the accuser, complainant, or critic. RECIPIENT is the accused. When the accusation appears inside a direct quotation, the ACTOR is the attributed speaker: if the text says the speaker spoke on behalf of an organization, the organization is the ACTOR, and if a titled officeholder speaks in his own name, the ACTOR is that person with the title. LOCATION is where the statement was made, else empty.

event_text: Shuttle Astronauts Finish First Spacewalk. Astronauts on the space shuttle have completed the first of their three scheduled spacewalks for tests on shuttle components and repair work on the International Space Station. Japanese astronaut Soichi Noguchi and his American crewmate Steve Robinson returned to the shuttle Saturday after a six-hour and 50-minute excursion. They tested repair techniques on the shuttle's thermal protection system and performed several repair tasks on the International Space Station, where the shuttle docked on Thursday. On future spacewalks they are to do more work on the space station before planned return to Earth on August 7. This week, NASA said insulating foam from the shuttle's external fuel tank may have struck the orbiter's wing on lift-off, but caused no serious damage. NASA has grounded further flights until the foam problem can be resolved. Loose foam doomed the shuttle in 2003 when a piece punched a hole in the wing during take-off. The shuttle broke apart during re-entry, killing all seven astronauts aboard.

## Event Type: ## Event: **AGREE**: Agree to, offer, promise, or otherwise indicate willingness or commitment to cooperate, including promises to sign or ratify agreements. This can include:

- Promise to sign a treaty
- Expressing willingness to meet in the future

- Express willingness to end a conflict

event_text: US Auditors Issue Afghan Report. A U.S. government oversight agency says Afghanistan's reconstruction program has no coherent spending strategy to implement its goals. A report by the U.S. Congress's Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction released late Thursday says the U.S. has appropriated, but not fully spent, $32 billion for humanitarian aid in the country, while other nations have donated $25 billion. The report found that reconstruction efforts have been fragmented and lack a central plan to complete U.S. goals. Those goals include rebuilding Afghan infrastructure, re-establishing political institutions, providing services to the Afghan people, and maintaining security necessary for reconstruction projects. The report also says government officials in Afghanistan want a greater say in building plans. Congress created the Office of the Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction under the authority of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2008. The measure was signed into law one year ago.

## Event Type: ## Event: **AID**: All provisions of providing material aid whose material benefits primarily accrue to the recipient.
